title: Council Unanimously Approves Data Center Moratorium
key_facts: The Milwaukee Common Council on Tuesday (13 Oct 2026) unanimously approved a one-year moratorium on new data center development, passing 13-0.
The moratorium generally bars construction of new data centers or expansion of existing ones while the city writes permanent zoning rules covering noise, energy use, water use and air quality.
Developers can still seek site-specific planned development zoning changes, which require public hearings and approval by the City Plan Commission and the Common Council.
It expires after one year or when permanent rules are adopted, whichever is first; state law allows a six-month extension.
Lead sponsor Ald. Marina Dimitrijevic said the council wants to find 'the right regulatory rules'; Mayor Cavalier Johnson supports it.
Opponents including the Metropolitan Milwaukee Association of Commerce and Building Advantage argued a moratorium could discourage investment, jobs and tax revenue.
The push followed public opposition that led to a 19,000-square-foot data center being dropped from a Walmart redevelopment; the moratorium applies to facilities of any size.
Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson has also called for a moratorium; large campuses by Microsoft and Vantage Data Centers are being built on the rural fringes of the Milwaukee region.
quote_evidence: The Milwaukee Common Council on Tuesday unanimously approved a one-year moratorium on new data center development, giving city officials time to establish permanent zoning regulations for the rapidly evolving industry.
“We are committed to finding the right regulatory rules,” she said.
The measure passed on a 13-0 vote, with council members Robert Bauman and JoCasta Zamarripa excused from the meeting.
why_it_matters_hint: A big US city has paused all new data centers for a year while it writes rules for noise, power, water and air quality.
notes: Single local outlet; vote count and mayor's support are stated in the article.
